authority: User clarifications and supplied DuTraveller screenshots, 2026-10-23
network_contract: MultiplayerGameplayContract.json: progression, inventory/equipment and skills must use server-authoritative mutations and appropriately scoped replication; captured design is not a claim of completed implementation.
confirmed_rules: Spell and talent trees provide class or skill-path references; players can combine skills across those paths as they level up.
Do not impose mutually exclusive Mage/Warrior player classes or class-based skill restrictions.
Player level/progression governs access to combinations. Preserve evidenced point-spending rules and recover additional requirements from original evidence.
Learning or upgrading a skill, assigning it to a slot, and activating it are distinct operations.
Restore the connection between the abilities screen's equipped skills and the gameplay hotbar.
Keep active/offensive slots and passive slots distinct. Recover slot compatibility and passive application behavior from original evidence.
Players can spend attribute points to permanently increase base primary attributes. Attribute points and spell/skill points are separate progression balances.

The supplied Attributes screen shows spend controls for Strength, Intelligence, Vigor, Defence, Resilience and Luck, with a separate Secondary Attributes section. Preserve serialized identifiers when UI spelling differs from code tags.
Equipment worn by the player can add bonuses to the player's base stats. Carrying an item in inventory alone does not establish that its equipment bonus is active.

Track permanent/base attributes separately from equipment contributions so equipping, swapping and unequipping can apply and remove the correct bonuses without corrupting permanent progression. Recover additive, percentage, stacking and derived-stat rules from original evidence.
screenshot_observations: Abilities screen contains Spell Tree, Talent Tree, Spell Points, Spend Point, Equip, current description and next-level description.
The illustrated active slot labels include LMB, RMB and 1 through 9; passive slots appear separately.
Gameplay images show the skill hotbar, passive indicators, resource orbs, minimap and different equipped character appearances.
Images have differing HUD layouts and some debugging/compile messages. They document design and prior running states, not proof that this local snapshot currently works.
do_not_infer: Exact spell damage, costs, cooldowns, level gates, prerequisites, rank limits or refund rules from icons alone.
A complete roster of exclusive player classes from widget names such as Mage or Warrior.
Class-specific model or equipment restrictions without supporting evidence.
That every historical screenshot uses the same finalized number of passive slots or HUD layout.
Attribute point awards per level, points required per increase, attribute increment size, caps, reset rules or derived-stat formulas from screenshot values alone.
restoration_acceptance: One player can retain and equip learned skills from more than one tree when progression requirements are met.
Spending a skill point updates the learned rank and both description panels consistently.
Equipping updates the selected hotbar slot and its input binding without removing unrelated learned skills.
Hotbar activation invokes the assigned skill with its actual resource, cooldown, animation and effect behavior.
Passive assignment applies and removes the appropriate effect exactly once, once its intended rules are recovered.
Learned skills, ranks and slot assignments survive save/reload according to the original persistence rules.

Spending attribute points validates the available balance, deducts the configured cost and applies the configured permanent base-attribute increase exactly once; insufficient points do not change either value.
Attribute-point spending updates dependent secondary stats and the attribute/HUD displays according to recovered formulas, independently of spell-point spending.
Unspent attribute points and purchased base-attribute increases survive save/reload and remain intact after equipment swaps.
Equipping applies the item's stat contribution once; swapping removes the previous item's contribution and applies the replacement; unequipping removes only that item's contribution.
Stat-dependent resource limits, combat values and HUD displays update consistently after equipment changes. Recover current-resource adjustment rules from evidence.
Loading an equipped item restores its bonuses exactly once and does not accumulate extra bonuses across reloads.
